newsitem.title: USA: Edison says it may extend Calif. nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: Edison says it may extend Calif. nuke outage.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co said Friday the current refueling outage at its 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit may need to be extended for additional repairs to the unit's two steam generators.
The unit was shut April 11 and is scheduled to restart in late June.

Edison said Friday inspections of the steam generators include examination of structural supports for some 9,000 small tubes which transfer heat from the reactor coolant to the water which becomes steam to power the turbine generator.

Initial inspections of these structural supports revealed several areas where the thickness of the supports had been significantly reduced, apparently by erosion during normal plant operation, the utility said.
Edison noted the cause of the condition is under investigation and the effect of the erosion on the strength of the supports is being analyzed to determine if any further action is required.
The ongoing refueling outage is scheduled for 75 days, but additional actions could be required which might extend the outage, the utility said.
Edison expects to conduct analysis and inspections during the next three weeks to determine if this is likely and to provide an estimate.
San Onofre's 1,070 MW unit 2 recently completed an inspection of its steam generators, and similar tube supports showed no signs of the erosion described above, Edison said.
Edison owns 75 percent of the San Onofre plant, with minority shares held by San Diego Gas & Electric Co and two municipal utilities.
